themes: New entrants: Birla Opus (Grasim) and JSW Dulux (ex-Akzo Nobel India)

Birla Opus booked Rs 1,661 cr of paint revenue in Q1FY27 (+64% YoY) and calls itself the No.3 organised decorative player; Investec puts its share gain at ~3-4% in two years. JSW took control of Akzo Nobel India in Dec-2025. Berger's MD: share lost 'mostly to Birla'; intensity 'reduced, but it still remains at an elevated level' (Aug-2026).
Input costs and prices (West Asia conflict, crude, TiO2)

Petroleum derivatives are 55-60% of paint inputs. The industry raised prices 14-16% in stages over Mar-Jun 2026; Brent fell ~15% in June. Price cuts usually come 3-4 months after inputs fall and are smaller than the rises (ICICI Securities, Jun-2026), but a cut before or after Diwali is the main risk to FY27-28 value growth.
FY26 was hurt by a long, heavy monsoon and an early Diwali; Q4FY26 standalone volume +11.8%, Q1FY27 +8.4% with drier weather and a later Diwali. Q2 volume guided at 7.5-8%.
Mix: construction chemicals, waterproofing, tile adhesives, economy emulsions

Construction chemicals are ~10-12% of Berger's decorative sales and grow much faster than paint, but they are low-price-per-kg products; with downtrading to economy emulsions they opened a 5-8pp gap between volume and value growth in FY25-26.
Industrial coatings: autos, infrastructure, government capex
GST on two-wheelers and cars cut from 28% to 18% helped automotive coatings; Union Budget FY27 public capex Rs 12.2 lakh cr supports protective coatings, where Berger is No.1.

India uses ~4.1 kg of paint per person vs 13-15 kg globally; the unorganised sector is still nearly a quarter of the market (AR FY26). Capacity added by new entrants speeds up formalisation but also caps pricing.

moat: Brand
Moderate

No.2 decorative brand with ~20% share of listed players, but Asian Paints is ~3x its size; Berger's ad spend is 'on par' with its market share while Birla Opus spends far above its share (MD, Feb-2026). A new corporate-brand campaign launched in Q1FY27.
Recognised, not dominant: it does not set prices.
Distribution and influencers
Moderate

64,475 dealers (11,100+ added in FY26), 10,000+ tinting machines a year, ~1,900 stores; clear leader in the North-East and strong in the East. But Birla Opus built 1,450+ franchise outlets and a No.3 position in about two years.
Valuable, but shown to be copyable with enough capital.
Pricing power
Weak

Standalone value growth was −0.4% to +6.7% in the eight quarters to Q4FY26 while volume grew 4-12%; economy-emulsion prices were cut; 2026 price rises followed the leader and the challenger. Realised price in Q1FY27 was ~5% against a 12-13% list-price rise.
Margins depend on the industry staying rational.
Cost position and backward integration
Neutral

Emulsions and most resins made in-house; high standalone gross margin (39-42%); mega plants at Panagarh and Khordha planned. Asian Paints is integrating further back and the new entrants have new, large plants.
No lasting cost edge either way.
Industrial niches (protective, automotive JV)
Strong advantage
No.1 in Indian protective coatings; automotive and coil coatings through JVs with Nippon Paint and Becker; industrial is ~18% of sales. New entrants are decorative-only.
A real niche, but too small to carry the group.
Customer switching costs
Weak
Homeowners rarely know the brand they buy; painters and dealers choose, and dealer schemes (10% free material, rebates) sway them.
Share can move with trade spending.
critiques: For two years Berger grew volume, not value: standalone volume +4-12% a quarter but value −0.4% to +6.7% (FY25-Q4FY26), from cheaper mix and price cuts
Share has stopped rising: ~20% of listed players; the MD conceded a 0.2pp loss in 9MFY26, 'mostly to Birla'
Q1FY27's double-digit value growth is price-led; prices may be cut once crude falls, as in past cycles, and dealer rebates were already rising
ICICI Securities via Business Today (Jun-2026); MD (Aug-2026)
EBITDA margin has been stuck at 15-17% (15.4% in FY26, EBITDA −1%), below Asian Paints' ~19-21%
A Rs 1,800-2,000 cr plant build-out arrives while the industry is adding a lot of capacity; returns on it depend on volumes the new entrants are fighting for
Bears: Morgan Stanley (Underweight, Rs 429) and Macquarie (Underperform, Rs 425) see weak industry growth visibility and elevated competition
Bulls: 'peak competitive intensity may be over' (Investec) and Birla Opus raised prices more than peers (ICICI Securities); Berger gains from stores and tinting machines
gaps: Berger reports one segment: decorative and industrial margins are not disclosed, and the decorative/industrial split is disclosed only for FY26 (industrial 18%); earlier years and quarterly splits are not available, so the business-line build starts from FY26.
